Continuous Cough and Snoring Monitoring Device

Design and verification of a device for continuous monitoring and categorization of cough and snoring using acoustic signals.

Project overview

The project aimed to design and validate a device capable of continuously monitoring and classifying cough and snoring from acoustic signals. The concept was intended to support remote follow-up by allowing health professionals to review recorded information.

The academic project focused on building a prototype that acquired audio signals, processed them and displayed the classification results on a computer.

Design and implementation

  • Signal Acquisition: Assembled an audio acquisition circuit using a unidirectional piezoelectric microphone, an LM386 amplifier and an Arduino microcontroller.
  • Embedded Electronics: Converted the analogue microphone signal into digital data and used LEDs to provide a visual indication of detected events.
  • Mechanical Design: Designed a plastic enclosure in Autodesk Inventor and manufactured it using 3D printing. The enclosure was intended to be worn with an adjustable chest strap, with the microphone attached near the neck.
  • Data Processing: Used Arduino and LabVIEW to acquire, process, filter, display and classify acoustic data.
  • Classification: Developed a conditional algorithm based on waveform characteristics, including amplitude and event duration, to distinguish cough from snoring.
  • Measurement Validation: Conducted repeatability and reproducibility analysis. The reported measurement variation was 1.43%, and the study reported 97.4% overall confidence in the collected data.
  • Prototype Verification: Evaluated the prototype using 50 cough samples and 50 snoring samples.

Prototype limitations and next steps

The Bluetooth connection was explored but was not retained in the final prototype because it reduced the quality and reliability of data acquisition. The project identified wireless operation and further validation with real users as future development steps.
